citations.text:
[s0-p2] In this paper we present our work, which is a part of the SociaL Media And Harassment
Competition of the ECML PKDD 2019 Conference. The topic of the competition is the classification of
different types of harassment and it is divided in two tasks. The first one is the classification of the tweets
in harassment and non-harassment categories, while the second one is the classification in specific
harassment categories like indirect harassment, physical and sexual harassment as well. We are using
the dataset of the competition, which includes text from tweets having the aforementioned categories.

[s2-p0] The dataset from Twitter that we are using in our work, consists of a train set, a validation set and
a test set. It was published for the "First workshop on categorizing different types of online harassment
languages in social media". The whole dataset is divided into two categories, which are harassment and
non-harassment tweets. Moreover, considering the type of the harassment, the tweets are divided into
three sub-categories which are indirect harassment, sexual and physical harassment. We can see in
Table TABREF1 the class distribution of our dataset. One important issue here is that the categories of
indirect and physical harassment seem to be more rare in the train set than in the validation and test sets.
